sect1.title: Achieving Multilib
sect1.para: Following the LFS principle, most software will be compiled from source. To be able to compile 32-bit libraries on 64-bit, a specific process must be performed. This process arms a 64-bit LFS system with a compiler that can compile 32-bit software, but will also arm the system with basic 32-bit libraries that a lot of software will require.

That process is detailed in Multilib LFS, also referred to as MLFS. The book, a version of LFS, can be read here. It's important to keep in mind that it is a version of LFS, not supplementary material. It doesn't arm an already existing 64-bit LFS system with a compiler that can target 32-bit software. It instead creates a new 64-bit LFS system that meets the goal of multilib. It is planned for a supplemental version of MLFS to eventually be made so users don't have to start from scratch in that regard, but for now, you will need to create a new LFS system using MLFS. If you already have a 64-bit only LFS system, you will need to start over.

The same principles of targeting 32-bit in that book will also apply to this book as well. If you haven't already, read to check what basic principles still apply in this book when targeting 32-bit. Furthermore, read to find out which instructions to follow.
